title: EconAgent: Large Language Model-Empowered Agents for Simulating Macroeconomic Activities

key_points.claim: Existing ABM agents use fixed rules or learned neural networks. Customizing each agent is hard, which makes heterogeneity difficult to model.
key_points.evidence_quote: customizing each agent presents significant challenges, complicating the modeling of agent heterogeneity

key_points.claim: Prior ABMs often overlook multi-period market dynamics and multifaceted macroeconomic factors in agent decisions.
key_points.evidence_quote: the influence of multi-period market dynamics and multifaceted macroeconomic factors are often overlooked

key_points.claim: EconAgent is an LLM-driven agent. The environment has market dynamics driven by agents' work and consumption decisions.
key_points.evidence_quote: a simulation environment that incorporates various market dynamics driven by agents’ decisions regarding work and consumption

key_points.claim: A perception module creates heterogeneous agents with distinct decision-making mechanisms.
key_points.evidence_quote: Through the perception module, we create heterogeneous agents with distinct decision-making mechanisms.

key_points.claim: A memory module lets agents reflect on past experience and market trends, which captures how macro trends affect decisions.
key_points.evidence_quote: a memory module, which allows agents to reflect on past individual experiences and market dynamics

key_points.claim: Experiments report more realistic decisions and more reasonable macro phenomena than rule-based or learning-based agents. The code is released.
key_points.evidence_quote: EconAgent can make realistic decisions, leading to more reasonable macroeconomic phenomena compared to existing rule-based or learning-based agents

reliability_notes: Abstract only. The fetch returned the ACL Anthology landing page, not the full text (PDF at aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.829.pdf). Peer-reviewed at ACL 2024. No quantitative results are given in the abstract.
